sampling_model.design: An independent sample \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is drawn from the selected multinomial law \(q\); an optional COPAG confidence set is produced from the same sample by a coverage-valid discovery procedure.
sampling_model.units: Each sampled unit is one retained clinical visit with finite coded variables \(V\); the population SCM also contains the binary selection variable \(S\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query is the hard intervention \(do(B=b)\); the intervention is hypothetical and sampling randomness comes from the selected observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every selected cell is positive under \(q\). The common lower bound \(\delta\) on population and post-intervention selection is a calibrated sensitivity restriction, not a standard overlap label; the conditional estimand itself only requires \(d_M>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(q\) by a simultaneous multinomial confidence region and propagate graph uncertainty by union over a COPAG confidence set; no faithfulness assumption is imposed on the identification class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 use finite disturbance-response models and polynomial optimization for a fixed canonical DAG; the graph-permitted NPSEM class does not require every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.

The PAG-compatible optimization concerns faithful no-selection SCMs; its edge semantics are generally incomparable with exact actual-parent semantics under positive but potentially unfaithful selection.
Theorem 4.13 identifies marginal DAG models with the same latent projection and Proposition 7.3 commutes intervention with projection, without proving closure of an exact actual-parent stratum.
Proposition 2 gives sourcewise finite-cardinality reduction preserving observed network behavior, not strict essential-source incidences.

Selected-marginalized directed graphs characterize normalized selected interventional indistinguishability, without retaining the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities calibrated here.

Theorem 4.15 supplies a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm and calculus on specified model classes; the paper distinguishes \(\mathcal M(G)\) from the positive discrete class \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), whose positivity conditions are not implied by positivity of the selected observed law \(q\).
Theorem 5 gives nonemptiness, openness, and density of faithful distributions in its total-variation Markov model, not an equal-moment legal lift on an unfaithful exact-graph boundary.
Criterion inversion yields consistent set estimators, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets defined by population minimizers.
Width-adaptive endpoint intervals attain uniform asymptotic coverage for an interval-identified scalar as identification width approaches zero.
Resampling and screening followed by a union of graph-specific intervals gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after causal discovery.

body.tldr: The exact actual-parent COPAG fiber for a positive, potentially unfaithful selected law is not proved closed.  What is established is a bounded finite graph-legal response fiber indexed by at most \(N!\) saturated orders, with essential-feature signs that exactly determine its selected MAG and singly exponential one-block real-algebraic certificates for its endpoint membership.  Independently of graph restrictions, consistency and the two calibrated selection margins give a universal closed-form outer envelope; one-source complete-COPAG witnesses attain it, and any permitted family containing those witnesses inherits the interval by sandwiching.  The binary interval \(\left[1/20,39/40\right]\) is an audit instance, not the headline.  Confidence-fiber inference provides finite-sample outer coverage for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery use case of Lee et al., while universal legal lifting remains open.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm on specified model classes; Yang et al. optimize over faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; Duarte et al. optimize a fixed canonical DAG; and Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models. None settles whether the exact actual-parent COPAG fiber for a positive, potentially unfaithful selected law is closed or has attained endpoints. This note also leaves that general question open, while formalizing it and proving bounded-finite and saturated special-case results.
project_justification.niche: The tractable object constructed here is the bounded finite graph-legal response fiber, a finite union of semialgebraic strata. Its essential-feature signs determine the exact selected MAG of each enumerated bounded response point. For each algebraic boundary value of the bounded image, the real-algebraic procedure decides membership in that bounded image and returns either a satisfying bounded branch or certificates that every bounded branch is empty. Equality with, and closure or attainment of, the full arbitrary-SCM fiber remain exactly \(\text{oeq:universal-legal-lifting}\).
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and exact polynomial legality test, embeds finite response architectures into at most \(N!\) saturated ordered superarchitectures, and gives singly exponential one-block endpoint certificates for the bounded finite image.  It proves a graph-free universal selection-margin envelope with one-source complete-COPAG attainment, designates the compelled-collider case as the first unresolved kill test, and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence for the arbitrary-SCM fiber.

body.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning.  Evans canonicalizes margins of latent DAGs and relates latent projection to intervention, but does not prove closure of an exact functional-essentiality stratum.  Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give network hidden-variable cardinality bounds; their sourcewise reduction motivates the finite support step but does not preserve strict actual-edge witnesses.  Duarte et al. fix a canonical DAG and optimize over graph-permitted finite NPSEMs, without requiring every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.  Yang et al. treat faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; their edge semantics and the actual-parent, potentially unfaithful selected-MAG semantics here are generally incomparable.  Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models, whereas the present margins constrain absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities.  Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm and calculus on specified model classes and distinguish \(\mathcal M(G)\) from the positive discrete class \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); positivity of the selected observed law \(q\) here is not equated with all positivity conditions defining \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not supply an equal-moment lift at an unfaithful boundary.  Basu supplies the real-algebraic sign-sampling and one-block elimination algorithms used for bounded-compiler certification.  Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky motivate confidence-set inversion, while the formal inference result here is only finite-sample outer coverage.  Lee et al. are the clinical consumer: their survivor-conditioned cardiac-surgery analysis uses FCI and LV-IDA under acknowledged selection bias and graph ambiguity.
body.interpretation: The graph-free theorem proves that every recursive SCM satisfying selected-law fit and the explicit inequalities \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\) and \(d_M\ge\delta\) lies in \([L_\delta,U_\delta]\). Separately, it constructs a one-source family in the complete all-circle COPAG class attaining every value of this interval. Equality therefore transfers only to a family of recursive SCMs that satisfies the graph-free premises and contains those stated witnesses. By contrast, the algebraic endpoint procedure concerns only the bounded finite graph-legal image: a positive certificate attains a value within that image, whereas a negative certificate excludes only its enumerated bounded branches and says nothing about nonattainment over arbitrary SCMs.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Saturated order-indexed superarchitectures remove redundant subset enumeration but do not close the legality topology.  In the positive binary exclusive-or family, moment-preserving support deletion can send a shared-source essentiality polynomial to zero while holding the selected law and intervention moment fixed.  An equal-moment legal lift exists in that example, so it is a warning against naive compression rather than a negative answer.  More generally, a bounded-compiler exclusion certificate does not exclude a repair outside the finite support bound.
body.honest_scope: Established results cover child-set source merging within the retained-variable response language, sourcewise moment-preserving finite support on a fixed permitted architecture, embedding into at most \(N!\) saturated ordered superarchitectures, exact polynomial legality for bounded finite response models, singly exponential existential-semialgebraic endpoint certification for that bounded image, a universal selection-margin outer envelope with exact complete-COPAG subclass attainment and sandwich transfer, and finite-sample confidence-fiber event inclusion.  Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded compiler, preservation of exact actual-parent semantics through arbitrary canonicalization or compression, and closure or attainment of the full positive-unfaithful COPAG fiber remain open.  No general endpoint-convergence claim is made.  The interval \(\left[1/20,39/40\right]\) is a binary audit instance, not evidence for universal lifting.
